Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: King of Great Britain Edward VII (author, Wikidata Q20875), died 1910; James Macaulay (editor, Wikidata Q16856581), died 1902. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Edward VII, King of Great Britain, 1841-1910; Macaulay, James, 1817-1902 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Speeches and addresses of H. R. H. the Prince of Wales: 1863-1888, London : J. Murray, 1889, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/speechesaddresse00edwaiala. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 100%, 100%, 88% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of King of Great Britain Edward VII, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
